:::{#exm-imaginary-unit-powers}
#### Powers of the imaginary unit

The powers of $i$ repeat in a cycle of four:

$$
\ba
i^3
&= i^2 \cd i
&& \text{(split off one factor of } i \text{)}
\\
&= (-1) \cd i
&& \text{(@def-imaginary-unit)}
\\
&= -i
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

and

$$
\ba
i^4
&= i^2 \cd i^2
&& \text{(split the power into two squares)}
\\
&= (-1) \cd (-1)
&& \text{(@def-imaginary-unit, twice)}
\\
&= 1
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

so the cycle starts again:

$$
\ba
i^5
&= i^4 \cd i
&& \text{(split off one factor of } i \text{)}
\\
&= 1 \cd i
&& \text{(} i^4 = 1 \text{)}
\\
&= i
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

and the powers run $i, -1, -i, 1, i, \ldots$.

:::
